info.text:
About 9 in 10 actively managed large-cap funds trailed the S&P 500 over the 15 years to June 2026, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices' SPIVA scorecard. This step-by-step guide explains what an index fund is (S&P 500 vs total market, mutual fund vs ETF), what comes first (an emergency fund and high-interest debt), the account choices with 2026 limits (401(k) $24,500, IRA $7,500; check IRS.gov for 2027), opening and funding an account, comparing expense ratios, automating, rebalancing and riding out drops like 2008 (-37%) and 2022 (-18%). A hypothetical example shows how a 0.03% vs 1% fee changes $10,000 a year over 30 years at an assumed 7%. No fund picks and no predictions.

Sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices SPIVA U.S. Mid-Year 2026 (Sept 2026) and Year-End 2025 scorecards; ICI, Trends in the Expenses and Fees of Funds, 2025 (March 2026); ICI Investment Company Fact Book 2025 and 2026; IRS Notice 2025-67 (Nov 2025) and IRS Roth IRA income limits for 2026; Federal Reserve SHED report (May 2026) and G.19 Consumer Credit (Oct 2026); SIPC; SEC Investor Bulletin on ETFs; Morningstar; S&P 500 total returns via S&P Dow Jones Indices; Reuters/NPR (March 28, 2013).

News and education, not financial advice.
